title: Buy-entry concurrency: double buys of one token and risk limits across concurrent handlers

options.name: Keep current behaviour: check at handler start, record after landing
options.risk: Two handlers for one token both buy (2x spend), and a burst of new tokens can pass the cooldown, position and exposure limits together.

options.name: Claim the token and reserve the risk budget synchronously before the first await; re-check inside the nonce lock
options.behavior_impact: At most one buy per token; limits hold under bursts; claims and reservations are released on a proven fail-clean.
options.risk: A claim that is never released (crash, bug) blocks that token or budget until restart; needs a clear release path.

options.name: Run the whole buy pipeline one token at a time per chain
options.behavior_impact: No concurrency at all on the buy side.
options.risk: Slow checks (30 s Mint wait, provider timeouts) delay every other opportunity on that chain.

options.name: Only re-check isTokenSniped and the limits inside the nonce lock
options.behavior_impact: Stops the second same-token buy if the first already inserted its row.
options.risk: Does not stop it when the first has not inserted yet, and does not fix risk-limit bursts.

recommendation: sync-claim-and-reserve, plus an in-flight guard on the HTTP pollers (TH-BUY-10) so one event is never dispatched twice.
default: Keep current behaviour until the owning phase decides (milestone contract). This card covers S0/S1 capital findings, which cannot rest on the default: until it is decided and fixed it blocks the live re-entry gate.
behavior_impact: Decides how many buys can be in flight at once and how limits are enforced under bursts.
needed_by: Phase 24 discussion (capital fixes, after the Phase 23 real-path proof)
